description: Extract resolveSelfInvokeArgv as the single compiled/interpreted self-invoke primitive (positive /$bunfs/ signal only), delegate resolveOrchResolverCmd to it, and fix forkMonitor's dead retry-monitor child on compiled binaries, pinned by a real bun build --compile integration test.

officialDocsConsulted.version: current (repo requires Bun >= 1.2; empirical grounding on 1.3.13)
officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirms /$bunfs/ is the documented internal virtual-path prefix bun injects for embedded entries inside a bun build --compile executable, with no deprecation or prefix-change notice. Docs additionally document Bun.isStandaloneExecutable (the official runtime API for detecting compiled mode).
officialDocsConsulted.localConventionConflict: Official docs recommend Bun.isStandaloneExecutable for standalone detection, while the CAM-426 spec pins detection to the pure argv1.startsWith('/$bunfs/') signal so the helper stays a pure unit-testable function of (execPath, argv1); the implementer should note this trade in the run.ts/util comment during Step 5.5 rather than silently switching APIs.

userStories.title: Extract resolveSelfInvokeArgv primitive and delegate resolveOrchResolverCmd to it
userStories.description: As a cam developer, I need a single exported function under src/util/ that decides interpreted-vs-compiled self-invocation keyed only on the positive /$bunfs/ signal, with resolveOrchResolverCmd reduced to a thin shell-quoting wrapper over it, so that the compiled-binary self-invoke bug class has exactly one canonical fix site and a version-managed bun shim (e.g. bun-1.3) no longer misclassifies an interpreted run as compiled.
acceptanceCriteria: A new exported function resolveSelfInvokeArgv(execPath: string, argv1: string | undefined): string[] exists under src/util/ and is the single place in src/ deciding interpreted-vs-compiled self-invocation: compiled mode (argv1 !== undefined && argv1.startsWith('/$bunfs/')) returns [execPath]; interpreted mode returns [execPath, argv1 ?? 'cam']. Unit tests pin both branches plus the undefined-argv1 fallback. [oracle: bun test test/util]
The negative basename heuristic exists nowhere in src/ after this change. [oracle: file-assert ! grep -rn "basename(execPath) !== 'bun'" src/]

resolveOrchResolverCmd (src/commands/run.ts) delegates to resolveSelfInvokeArgv with no duplicated detection logic, and renders identical command strings for the two previously-correct cases: interpreted with a real script argv1 (3-token form) and compiled with a /$bunfs/ argv1 (2-token form). [oracle: bun test test/commands/run-orch-resolver-compiled-mode.test.ts]

The former Arm B behavior is inverted and tested: an interpreted run under a version-managed interpreter shim (execPath basename e.g. 'bun-1.3') with a real script argv1 now renders the interpreted 3-token form, not the collapsed compiled form; the test in test/commands/run-orch-resolver-compiled-mode.test.ts asserting collapse on basename alone is updated accordingly, and the new assertion is swept red-against-main before being trusted. [oracle: bun test test/commands/run-orch-resolver-compiled-mode.test.ts]

The run.ts comment block documenting Arm B as defense-in-depth is updated in the same commit to describe the positive-signal-only design and the deliberate trade (a future /$bunfs/ prefix change degrades to orch-resolve's loud fail-safe fallback instead of propagating a silent dead-child failure). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Lint spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: new src/util/self-invoke.ts (src/util/ currently holds only retry-pid.ts), src/commands/run.ts (resolveOrchResolverCmd at ~line 281, comment block ~lines 269-280, drop the basename arm at line 282; the basename import stays because run.ts uses it elsewhere for session naming), test/util/ new unit test, test/commands/run-orch-resolver-compiled-mode.test.ts (160 lines, currently asserts collapse on basename alone; invert that case). resolveOrchResolverCmd returns a shell-quoted STRING via q() while callers of the primitive need string[]: extraction is argv-level, the q()-joining stays in run.ts. Domain terms 'self-invoke primitive' and 'bunfs virtual entry' are already in CONTEXT.md (lines 416-420). Grounding: patterns.md bullets for US-003/US-R1-001 of CAM-425 (grep patterns.md for 'bunfs' / 'self-invoke'); test as a PURE unit per the US-R1-001 bullet. Doc conflict inherited from officialDocsConsulted: official Bun API Bun.isStandaloneExecutable exists; spec pins the pure argv1 /$bunfs/ prefix check for unit-testability; document the choice in the comment, do not switch APIs.

userStories.title: Fix forkMonitor's dead retry-monitor child via resolveSelfInvokeArgv
userStories.description: As a cam claude user on an installed compiled binary, I need forkMonitor to build its monitor-child argv through resolveSelfInvokeArgv so that the retry-monitor child (silently dead since 2026-05-14: it read the /$bunfs/ path as its command and exited 1 with 'unknown command') is revived on every compiled binary while staying correct interpreted.
acceptanceCriteria: forkMonitor (src/retry/launcher.ts) builds its child argv as [...resolveSelfInvokeArgv(process.execPath, process.argv[1]), 'retry-monitor', pane, String(claudePid)], with no local detection logic. [oracle: grep -q 'resolveSelfInvokeArgv' src/retry/launcher.ts]

Unit tests in test/retry/interactive.test.ts assert the FULL spawned argv (prefix included, full-array equality) for both shapes: interpreted (bun execPath + script argv1 => 5 tokens) and compiled (/$bunfs/ argv1 => 4 tokens, no script token). Asserting only argv[0] plus the trailing 3 tokens is no longer sufficient anywhere in the file; the compiled-shape assertion is swept red-against-main (it fails against the old [self, mainScript, ...] construction). [oracle: bun test test/retry/interactive.test.ts]

The patterns.md US-R1-001 bullet naming forkMonitor as a plausible follow-up target is updated in the same commit to record that forkMonitor now shares the primitive. [oracle: file-assert ! grep -q 'plausible follow-up target' scripts/cam/patterns.md]
The ported-file MIT license header at the top of src/retry/launcher.ts remains intact. [oracle: grep -q 'License: MIT' src/retry/launcher.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Lint spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: src/retry/launcher.ts (forkMonitor at line 224; buggy construction at lines 238-239: const mainScript = process.argv[1] ?? 'cam'), test/retry/interactive.test.ts (existing tests assert only argv[0] and argv.slice(-3), the exact blind spot that let the bug survive; close it, do not preserve it), scripts/cam/patterns.md (US-R1-001 CAM-425 bullet, grep for 'plausible follow-up target'). Gotcha from spec: the issue title says 'cam retry' but no such command exists; forkMonitor's only call site is src/commands/claude.ts:146 inside launchClaudeInteractive, so the affected user-facing command is cam claude (interactive, inside tmux); print mode never touches forkMonitor. Bun injects the /$bunfs/ virtual entry as the CHILD's argv[1] automatically in compiled mode, so the spawned argv must NOT include a script token there; index.ts main() dispatches on argv[2] in both modes. Out of scope (per spec): post-spawn liveness checks on the detached unref'd monitor child; adjacent cam resume defects (filed separately by fix-site policy).

userStories.title: Pin the /$bunfs/ compiled self-invoke premise with a real compiled-binary integration test
userStories.description: As a cam maintainer, I need an integration test that compiles a real fixture with bun build --compile and proves the self-invoke round-trip in both compiled and interpreted modes, so that the /$bunfs/ premise resolveSelfInvokeArgv keys on is pinned empirically repo-wide and a future bun prefix change fails loudly in CI instead of silently killing self-spawned children.
acceptanceCriteria: An integration test performs a real bun build --compile of a small fixture entry importing resolveSelfInvokeArgv from src/, runs the compiled fixture, has it self-spawn [...resolveSelfInvokeArgv(process.execPath, process.argv[1]), '<marker-token>'], and asserts (a) inside the compiled binary process.argv[1] starts with '/$bunfs/' and (b) the spawned child observes the marker token at process.argv[2]. [oracle: bun test test/integration/self-invoke-compiled.test.ts]
The same fixture run interpreted (bun <fixture>.ts) also self-spawns, and the child likewise sees the marker at argv[2]. [oracle: bun test test/integration/self-invoke-compiled.test.ts]
The test builds into a tmpdir and cleans up its artifacts, including .bun-build temp files (CAM-407 leak class). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

The test is NOT skipIf-guarded: if bun compile is unavailable the test fails loudly (CAM-424 class: silent skipIfs make the suite lie). [oracle: file-assert ! grep -q 'skipIf' test/integration/self-invoke-compiled.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Lint spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: new test/integration/self-invoke-compiled.test.ts plus a small fixture entry (co-locate under test/integration/ per existing convention; dir already hosts real-subprocess tests like tmux-introspect.test.ts and commit-exists-real-git.test.ts as the pattern to follow). The fixture must import resolveSelfInvokeArgv from src/ (US-001 dependency) so the pinned premise is the production primitive, not a copy. Depends on US-001 only; independent of US-002. Use waitForCondition for async waits, never a fixed setTimeout (curated test-quality invariant). Compile with an explicit --outfile inside the tmpdir; clean the tmpdir and any .bun-build temp files in afterAll even on failure. Marker-token assertion is behavioral (child echoes its argv[2]); no mock-call-only assertions. Official Bun docs (see officialDocsConsulted) confirm /$bunfs/ as the documented internal prefix; this test is the repo-wide empirical pin against a future change.

findings.text: The new real-compile integration test runs at 3.89-3.93s (3 consecutive local runs, warm macOS arm64) against bun's 5000ms per-test default, and declares no explicit timeout. Phase profile: `bun build --compile` 1383ms + run-binary-plus-inner-self-spawn 2916ms, i.e. ~21% headroom on fast local hardware. CI runs the same `bun test` on macos-latest (.github/workflows/ci.yml:15), where writing and cold-executing a 63MB standalone binary is materially slower, so this is a live CI-timeout flake risk in a repo that already had to fix CI-load flakes (main a0478daa). Ten sibling integration tests already set an explicit `{ timeout: N }` (test/integration/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts:267 45_000, issue-file-on-main.test.ts:203 20_000, ship-finalize-dirty-prd.test.ts:177 20_000, orch-respawn-reresolve.test.ts:143 15_000). Fix: give both tests in the file an explicit timeout (e.g. `{ timeout: 30_000 }`), matching that convention.

The two monkeypatched tests restore `process.execPath` / `process.argv[1]` with plain statements after the `forkMonitor(...)` call instead of a try/finally. Assertions run after the restore so an assertion failure is safe, but a throw inside `forkMonitor` would leak a bogus global `process.execPath` into every later test in the same runner process. Wrapping the call in try/finally (or a small `withPatchedArgv(...)` helper shared by both tests) makes the restore unconditional.

Detection keys on the `/$bunfs/` argv1 prefix rather than Bun's documented `Bun.isStandaloneExecutable` (https://bun.com/docs/bundler/executables). Verified that the official API is genuinely unavailable on the repo's pinned runtime (`typeof Bun.isStandaloneExecutable === 'undefined'` on bun 1.3.13), so the prefix signal is correct today and the new integration test pins the premise. Worth revisiting as an optional injected default (e.g. a third `isStandalone` parameter defaulting to the Bun global) once the repo's .bun-version reaches a release that exposes it, so a future prefix change cannot silently re-kill forkMonitor's child.

Boundary coverage stops at `undefined` argv1. An empty-string argv1 (`resolveSelfInvokeArgv(execPath, '')`) currently yields `[execPath, '']`, injecting an empty argv token, whereas the `?? 'cam'` fallback covers only `undefined`. Unreachable in practice from `process.argv[1]`, but one more case would pin the intended contract.
